top.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Steelers’ Insider offers cryptic hint after shocking Aaron Rodgers benching appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Pittsburgh Steelers stunned the NFL late Tuesday night by benching four-time MVP Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph their starting quarterback for Friday’s clash against the Denver Broncos. Even more surprising, the team isn’t entirely sure how its veteran signal-caller will handle the move. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, Pittsburgh left Rodgers inactive despite a clean injury report and braced for the fallout. “The #Steelers do not know how Aaron Rodgers will react to tonight’s news,” Schultz reported. “‘I guess we’ll find out together,’ a source said.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The #Steelers do not know how Aaron Rodgers will react to tonight’s news. “I guess we’ll find out together,” a source said. https://t.co/OwZdKL1OJW pic.twitter.com/s6dCsePKbo — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 25, 2026 That uncertainty makes the timing even wilder. Just one day earlier on Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy publicly backed his 42-year-old quarterback, who turns 43 next week. McCarthy won a Super Bowl alongside Rodgers with the Green Bay Packers and reunited with him in Pittsburgh for what Rodgers called his 22nd and final NFL season. However, two straight losses dropped the Steelers to 6-4 and pushed the coaching staff to hit the reset button . Across 10 starts this year, Rodgers has completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions, posting a career-low 86.6 passer rating while taking 31 sacks. Sunday’s 19-16 road loss to the Philadelphia Eagles exposed Pittsburgh’s offensive stagnation. Rodgers completed 30 of 44 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown with zero interceptions, though Philadelphia’s pass rush sacked him five times. Pittsburgh didn’t find the end zone until Rodgers hit Max Hurleman , who led the team with six catches for 61 yards, for a 20-yard score with 1:21 remaining. Rodgers also led the Steelers with 29 rushing yards, while wideout DK Metcalf managed just one catch for two yards on four targets before officials ejected him for two personal fouls. Now, Pittsburgh hands the offense to Rudolph, who owns a 9-9-1 record across 19 career starts with the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, leaving Rodgers’ future in complete limbo. top.title: 'We can win without him!' - Hansi Flick insists Barcelona can cope with Lamine Yamal injury blow ahead of Champions League clash against Sabah
top.description: FC Barcelona v Villarreal CF - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona manager Hansi Flick has challenged his squad to prove they can thrive in the absence of Lamine Yamal as the teenage sensation sits out Wednesday's Champions League trip to Sabah. The 19-year-old has been the focal point of the Blaugrana's devastating attack this term, but an ankle issue has forced him to stay behind in Spain while his teammates travel to Azerbaijan. Ankle injury ends Yamal's ever-present run Yamal has started all 17 of Barcelona's games this season, scoring 13 goals and registering 13 assists, before missing out for the first time. Monday's medical checks prompted staff to leave the 19-year-old in Spain ahead of Baku trip , though he should return for Sunday's La Liga trip to Deportivo A Coruna. Flick has yet to finalise his attack for Wednesday's tie, with Karim Adeyemi, Gabriel Jesus, Anthony Gordon, and Raphinha all competing to deputise. Defensive injuries further complicate selection, as Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart remain out while Pau Cubarsí is unlikely to be risked following a hip problem. Flick and De Jong back squad depth At Tuesday's pre-match press conference, Flick downplayed Yamal's absence while praising De Jong's adaptability. "We have played without Lamine in the past, we know what to do," Flick said. "He is very important for us, but [on Monday] we checked and decided it is better he stays at home. Hopefully, everything works well and he's available for the weekend." Speaking earlier, De Jong - who has made five appearances since overcoming a knee injury - backed the squad's quality. "A player like Lamine will always be missed," the midfielder said. "He is a player with extraordinary talent. He creates danger and chances on his own, so you notice when a player like him is not there. But the squad is full of good players and we can win without him." With defensive shortages potentially keeping De Jong at centre-back , Flick applauded his selflessness. "The thing I like most about Frenkie is that he said 'OK, coach, if you need me as a centre-back or a full-back, it doesn't matter,'" Flick explained. "He said he's available and he can help the team. This is, for me, a team player. He gives everything for this team. "We all know he is one of the best midfielders in the world. I see him as a midfielder, we need his quality there, but at the moment we will see where we need him tomorrow." De Jong reiterated his long-term positional preference while putting the team first: "I consider myself a midfielder, everyone knows that. I have always played there. But if team needs me elsewhere or the coach considers it better I play in another position, I will always do it." Barca chase first European crown since 2015 Barcelona enter Wednesday's clash in commanding domestic form, leading La Liga with 12 wins from 13 games. Three victories from four Champions League outings have also fuelled hopes of a first European trophy since 2015.

top.title: How to unearth young stars, the Bayern Munich way
top.description: Bayern initially aim to find young players from Bavaria before looking further afield [Getty Images] Bayern Munich are one of the elite powers in European football and current home of Ballon d'Or winner and England captain Harry Kane. But, while Kane is the latest hugely successful foreign import at Bayern, the German giants also put a particular focus on producing their own elite young talent. In 2013, Bayern had four homegrown players in the starting line-up as they won the Champions League. Repeating that victory, and continuing the club's history of nurturing young players, is what director of youth development and campus Jochen Sauer says Bayern are aiming for. Sauer joined from RB Salzburg in 2017 when the academy campus opened in another part of Munich, away from the first-team training complex. The club's motto "Mia San Mia" translates to "we are who we are" and Sauer says it has always been the club's goal to have a local homegrown element in its senior side. "It was always our identity and philosophy to be a regional club, but at the same time to be competitive internationally and on Champions League level," Sauer tells BBC Sport. "But always having a core of our team coming from the Munich area and the Bavarian region with a deep identification with the club and the city. "Our recruitment guidelines, especially for the under-11 to the under-15 teams, is trying to recruit as much talent as possible from the Munich area and the region of Bavaria." Munich-born Croatia international Josip Stanisic is a good example. The midfielder, 26, signed as an under-17 player from local outfit SC Furstenfeldbruck, while 22-year-old Aleksandar Pavlovic joined the academy aged eight and has worked his way up to the first team and is a Germany international. But perhaps the biggest name to come out of the academy in recent times is Jamal Musiala. The former Chelsea youth player, who joined aged 16, is a star for Bayern and Germany and has already won six Bundesliga titles at just 23 years old. It was part of the club's strategy to bring in the best young foreign players, and those with German passports, to the club, but they also enjoyed a bit of luck. The move came around the time Bayern Munich were interested in then-Chelsea winger Callum Hudson-Odoi, who shared the same agent as Musiala, who moved from Germany to England when he was seven. Bayern were already aware of Musiala because he was born in Germany, but the timing was right to make a deal happen. "There were for sure some pieces that came together at that time," Sauer says. "I think one reason why we fought for the player at that time was the reason we had the feeling that Chelsea is not really seeing his full potential to be a top player for their first team. "Because, otherwise, if they would have seen him as a future prospect, then it would been hard, even for Bayern Munich, to get a player out of the Chelsea environment." top.title: Key Barcelona defender unlikely to start against Sabah despite being fit – report
top.description: Key Barcelona defender unlikely to start against Sabah despite being fit – report Pau Cubarsi is expected to start on the bench when Barcelona face Sabah in the Champions League later today, as Hansi Flick looks to protect the young centre-back following his recent muscular problem. According to Mundo Deportivo , the defender is available for selection, but the Barcelona manager would prefer to give him additional time to recover fully. The 19-year-old has already missed Barcelona’s recent fixture against Villarreal after suffering an iliopsoas overload during the recent international break. With the Catalans facing a demanding schedule , Flick is unlikely to take unnecessary risks with one of his most important defensive players. Flick prioritises Cubarsi’s recovery after injury Cubarsi sustained the problem during Spain’s match against England in the previous international break. Cubarsi could start on the bench against Sabah. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) He was forced to finish the game early , and subsequent tests confirmed an overload in his iliopsoas muscle, located in the hip region. The centre-back was subsequently left out of Barcelona’s starting lineup against Villarreal, with Flick opting for a makeshift defensive partnership instead. Speaking ahead of the Sabah match , Flick confirmed that Cubarsi could play but indicated that resting him would be the preferred option if the team could manage without him. “He can play, he’s available. It’s nothing serious, nothing major or dangerous, but perhaps he could rest a little longer. If we can manage without him, we will. If we need him, he’s available,” the German admitted. Barcelona consider defensive changes against Sabah In Cubarsi’s absence against Villarreal, Flick deployed Frenkie de Jong alongside Gerard Martin in central defence, while Eric Garcia operated at right-back. Pau Cubarsi did not play against Villarreal. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) That arrangement could change in Baku if Jules Kounde is available to return to the starting lineup. The French defender’s potential involvement would give Flick another option at right-back and allow him to reconsider Eric Garcia’s position. One possible arrangement would see Kounde occupy the right side of defence, with Eric Garcia partnering Gerard Martin in the centre. However, the final selection has not been confirmed, and Flick could still decide to retain De Jong in defence.

top.title: Eduard Löwen powers San Jose to first playoff win in 14 years
top.description: Eduard Löwen powers San Jose to first playoff win in 14 years By Harrison Hamm San Jose Earthquakes fans have been awaiting this moment for a generation. In the first-ever Audi MLS Cup Playoffs game at PayPal Park on Tuesday night, summer signing Eduard Löwen delivered a stunning long-range free kick that proved the difference in the Quakes' 2-1 win over Houston Dynamo FC , just a day after being named the 2026 MLS Comeback Player of the Year . The Game 1 victory in their Western Conference Round One Best-of-3 Series marked San Jose's first Audi MLS Cup Playoffs since 2012 and puts the Earthquakes one win away from advancing in the postseason for the first time since 2010. “We had a really good performance,” Löwen told Apple TV postgame. “We played well. We were the better team." Lovely Löwen With San Jose leading 1-0 courtesy of captain Ronaldo Vieira 's first MLS goal, Löwen unleashed one of the most impressive strikes of the playoffs so far. His free kick from distance caromed in off the post past Jonathan Bond , mere minutes after Bond had made a diving stop to deny another Löwen free kick. “It's definitely high up,” Löwen said of where the goal ranks in his career tallies. “It's definitely high up in the category. I'm thankful that the second one went in. Credit to the goalkeeper on the first one. That was an amazing save, and I thought I'd go the same way again. But then I thought maybe I'd try the other way." Since being acquired in August from St. Louis CITY SC , Löwen has established himself as an integral piece of the Quakes’ midfield, as he proved at both ends of the pitch on Tuesday night with a goal-line clearance to preserve San Jose's lead shortly before going on to double the advantage with his first playoff goal. Löwen's success in San Jose follows a time of significant personal adversity during which he stepped away from professional soccer last year to care for his wife, Ilona, who passed away in March after two years of brain cancer treatment. The German playmaker returned to the sport this season and has excelled, earning recognition as the Comeback Player of the Year. Now, he is helping lead the way as the Quakes look to go somewhere they haven’t been in more than a decade. “Everything’s new here,” legendary head coach Bruce Arena said after the game. “We’re learning to be a good club. We’re learning to be a good team. Anything where we’re moving in a good direction is positive.” Headed to Houston San Jose can close out the Round One Best-of-3 Series in Game 2 on Saturday at Shell Energy Stadium in Houston, where a win would send them to the Western Conference Semifinals (2:30 pm ET | Apple TV ). If Houston claim victory, it would force a decisive Game 3 back at PayPal Park on Dec. 2. “We're gonna take the win and go to Houston and try to end the series in Houston,” Arena said. “It's gonna be a hell of a battle.” WATCH: Eduard Löwen guides San Jose Earthquakes to Game 1 win over Houston

top.title: Why The NFL Is Bringing U2 And Wu-Tang Clan To Thanksgiving Football
top.description: The NFL logo is seen on the field. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty Images The NFL on Thanksgiving isn’t going to challenge the Super Bowl anytime soon But Thanksgiving offers something the Super Bowl does not: multiple games, more entertainment and a direct connection to holiday shopping. This year, for the first time, the NFL will air games on Thanksgiving Eve, Thanksgiving and Black Friday. And the games will create a large-scale entertainment platform for Wu-Tang Clan, U2, Miranda Lambert, and the Goo Goo Dolls, all of whom are performing in some capacity amid the five (count ‘em, five) games blitzing streaming and linear broadcast networks. The festivities begin when the Packers and Rams clash in the inaugural Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix. Here’s why the NFL on Thanksgiving is now the place to see the band that changed rap forever with Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers) : the NFL has already won the battle for sports fans. Thanksgiving week is about the NFL embedding itself into popular culture through entertainment and commerce, which attracts viewers beyond sports enthusiasts. From Doubleheaders to Dolly Parton The NFL has come a long way since Thanksgiving meant watching the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys square off against different opponents on network TV with nothing particularly noteworthy happening at halftime. Dolly Parton creating a cultural moment (and arguably eclipsing the game itself) by appearing in a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader uniform as she did in 2023 was unthinkable. But the tradition began to change over a period of years, beginning when the NFL added a third Thanksgiving game in 2006. The rise of streaming was the catalyst that pushed the NFL to another level of entertainment and football. The launch of Amazon’s Black Friday game in 2023 marked the first time the NFL expanded its holiday programming beyond Thanksgiving Day. And that year, the NFL began a sustained pattern of promoting three major musical headliners across all three Thanksgiving Day games. The streaming businesses have had good reason to muscle their way into the Thanksgiving tradition. The NFL is by far the most popular programming on American television, averaging roughly 18.7 million viewers per game during the 2025 regular season and continuing to draw huge audiences into the 2026 season. Streaming businesses, facing viewer saturation, need to monetize audiences more effectively with advertising, and advertising means competing with traditional television networks for the kinds of programming that attract large, predictable audiences. NFL football delivers those audiences at a time when retailers and consumer brands are spending heavily to capture holiday shoppers. Netflix also gives the NFL the means to export a distinctly American tradition to the rest of the world. The details came out in a long interview on The Grade Cricketer podcast, which was Khawaja's first major long-form conversation since Pat Cummins held a marathon press conference in Sydney, and since Bancroft published his own confession. Khawaja's memoir, Sabr, had reopened the 2018 ball-tampering scandal a few weeks earlier, and his claim that the whole team knew about it has divided the Australian dressing room ever since. top.title: Players in limbo after NZ netball league collapses
top.description: Mason has played professionally for six years [Getty Images] All Parris Mason has known is playing netball. But with a World Cup just nine months away, she and four other New Zealand players have been left in limbo after the collapse of their domestic league. "There's a high potential I will not be playing netball heading into a World Cup," she told BBC Sport. While a significant number of her Silver Ferns team-mates play professionally in Australia and England, Mason stayed with her home league. The 23-year-old defender, who has been a full-time professional for six years, found out her netball fate when the news was leaked to the media. "It shattered me," she said. "The influx of emotions; is my career over? What do I do next? It was just so much to handle all at once." Netball New Zealand admitted the way events unfolded publicly was deeply regrettable and has pledged to support the affected players. "We know this period of uncertainty has been extremely tough for players, coaches, teams and everyone involved in the domestic competition," a statement said. "Their wellbeing is our priority, and we are working closely with the New Zealand Netball Players' Association to support them." It comes as the Silver Ferns are on the cusp of becoming the world's number one ranked side, after winning gold at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and beating Australia in the Constellation Cup. The World Cup will be held in Sydney, Australia, between 25 August and 5 September, with New Zealand looking to win the title for a sixth time. What happened to the ANZ Premiership? There had been uncertainty over the future of the ANZ Premiership for a couple years. The league had struggled to secure long-term broadcast deals which impacted the league financially. In 2026, the league recorded a loss of around $NZ 3.7m (£1.5m). There was an exodus of the country's best players. Ten of the 12 Silver Ferns who won gold for New Zealand at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow have moved overseas to play - primarily in Australia. Businesswoman Anna Mowbray and her husband, former All Blacks player Ali Williams, pitched a new private league for 2027, but negotiations fell through just eight weeks after signing a term sheet. "I don't understand my life without netball," said Mason. "It's been a big part of my identity, and [there is a] mental toll to [being] continually knocked down. "I think of everything in this whole situation as just completely sad." Nathan Limm, who has been following the story for the New Zealand Herald said: "The Ferns' success feels a little bit fragile. top.title: Nick Wright’s Patrick Mahomes take gets trolled in his latest NFL quarterback ranking
top.description: Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images Nick Wright’s latest NFL quarterback rankings sparked a debate, where his Patrick Mahomes take got brutally trolled. Patrick Mahomes has done a brilliant job in recent weeks to keep a patched-up Kansas City Chiefs afloat by turning back the clock. He is clearly not ready to relinquish his throne as the quarterback to usurp in this league, but several contenders are gunning for it. Nick Wright felt that contendership and more after his latest Patrick Mahomes take got trolled by the whole studio. Nick Wright puts Patrick Mahomes top of the mountain Wright creates a “Mahomes Mountain” at the end of every gameweek in the NFL, and as the name suggests, it ranks the quarterbacks in the league. Being named Mahomes Mountain has nothing to do with the ranking of Mahomes, but Wright perhaps took the name a bit too literally in his latest ranking. Speaking on First Things First , Wright ranked the quarterbacks, and put Mahomes at the top, ahead of Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow in the tier just below. While Mahomes has undoubtedly been elite again this season, this take didn’t go down well with the rest of his studio, who vouched for Purdy to be at the top. It got so comedic that Wright’s own takes were replayed back to him, which he gave when the 49ers completed a dominant win against the Vikings, courtesy of a perfect Purdy performance. He said at the time that Purdy is the league MVP, which naturally means that he is the best quarterback in the league as well! Here’s what Wright said to justify placing Mahomes at the top: “He was a man who for the 2nd time in his career, just had a 4-game stretch, averaging 300 yards per game, averaging more than 3 touchdowns per game with no turnovers, which has only been done in his career by one other person, Aaron Rodgers.” Wright’s previous comments were immediately played back to him, and he played it off as choosing between two elites, saying two things swayed him – Broussard saying Purdy wasn’t the MVP, and him saying Purdy was the best quarterback in the NFC. How that makes sense is left up to the reader, because Wright didn’t seem very convinced about it either! top.title: ‘Got to be…’ – Maxx Crosby sounds off on Bijan Robinson’s take about the easiest position in the NFL
top.description: Credit: Emilee Chinn/Aric Becker / AFP via Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders DE Maxx Crosby did not appreciate Atlanta Falcons RB Bijan Robinson’s take that the edge rusher is the easiest position in the NFL. Every elite or contending team is looking to build their offence around a world-class QB and their defence around a world-class edge rusher. Defensive players usually play within a system, so the EDGE is the one defender who is designed to be an independent unit responsible for sacking a slow QB. Unfortunately, the limited scope of the role led to Falcons RB Robinson dismissing the position as the easiest in the NFL, irking standout EDGE Crosby. Maxx Crosby slams Bijan Robinson’s ‘casual a– take’ Crosby, a former All-Pro EDGE, responded to Robinson’s thoughts on ‘The Rush Podcast,’ justifying their value while tearing down the position Robinson stars in. “Casual a– take. Look at it like this: who is your highest-paid player (QB)? And who is next (EDGE)? If it were easy to play the position and get one sack a game, why doesn’t everybody do it? Out of 1,000 snaps, getting 10 sacks is great. You’re considered elite. Running back? You get handed the ball, and you go play football. You run, and you catch. Running back is, easily, got to be the easiest position to play.” It might be easier to be an average EDGE than an average RB, but the top-tier EDGEs are more valuable because of how scarce the talent at the highest level is, compared to productive RBs being more available. EDGEs also create plays actively detrimental to another team while having longer careers on average than RBs, so Crosby’s point cannot be ignored. What did Bijan Robinson say? Robinson spoke on the St. Brown Podcast, hosted by Lions RB Amon-Ra St. Brown, and shared his harsh take on edge rushers in the NFL. “I would say D-Line. Edge rusher. You have one job, get past the tackle. You don’t have too much responsibility, especially if you’re one who has to rush the passer, I would say that’s the easiest. top.title: Can We Prepare Children For Financial Success Before They Start Earning?
top.description: Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire on the importance of childhood financial literacy, the inspiration behind her book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , and her mission to raise a financially conscious generation. In a world where children are increasingly exposed to financial pressures, consumerism and unrealistic portrayals of wealth, teaching them how to manage money has become more important than ever. Yet, financial education remains largely absent from many children’s formative learning experiences. Following the launch of her children’s book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , economist, financial literacy advocate and author, Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire, speaks about the personal experiences that inspired the book, why financial education must begin in childhood and her vision of making financial literacy accessible to children across Nigeria and Africa. Why should financial education begin in childhood? Interviewer: Financial literacy is increasingly becoming an important conversation among adults. Why are you making a case for introducing it to children? Ufuoma Paula: I believe we have waited too long to introduce children to conversations about money. We spend years teaching them how to read, write, calculate and prepare for examinations, but how much attention do we give to preparing them to make sound financial decisions? A child can graduate with excellent grades and still have no idea how to budget, save towards a goal, distinguish between needs and wants or manage money responsibly. Financial literacy is not something people suddenly need when they get their first salary. It is a life skill that is best developed early. Children already interact with money. They receive pocket money, make spending choices, compare what they own with what their friends have and develop attitudes towards money from what they observe at home and in society. Whether we deliberately teach them or not, they are learning something about money every day. The question is whether what they are learning is preparing them for responsible financial decisions. The lessons children learn about money today can influence the financial habits, values and decisions they carry into adulthood. Those decisions will affect not only their personal wellbeing, but also their families, businesses and communities. When we raise financially informed individuals, we are contributing to a society where people are better equipped to make responsible choices, recognise opportunities and manage resources wisely. We should teach children not just how to make money someday, but how to manage resources, recognise opportunities, create value and understand that money is a tool, not a master. top.title: Pep Guardiola admits he was 'embarrassed' to reject Italy job as former Man City boss confirms national team management is his 'next step'
top.description: Bournemouth v Manchester City - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Pep Guardiola has broken his silence on his decision to turn down the opportunity to manage Italy, admitting he felt "embarrassed" to say no to the Azzurri. The legendary tactician, currently on a sabbatical following a trophy-laden decade at Manchester City, also confirmed that his next move in football will be onto the international stage. Italy approached Guardiola after third straight World Cup miss In July, after Italy missed a third consecutive World Cup, the Italian federation (FIGC) sent Paolo Maldini and Leonardo to approach Guardiola . The offer arrived shortly after he left Manchester City following a 2016–2026 stint yielding six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and a Champions League crown. Drained by the grind, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich manager chose a self-imposed sabbatical of at least one year. Italy subsequently re-hired Roberto Mancini , their Euro 2020-winning coach from 2018 to 2023. Guardiola opens up on emotional Azzurri refusal Speaking on Romario TV on Tuesday with Brazil legend and former Barcelona team-mate Romario, Guardiola explained why timing scuppered the Italy move. He also confirmed his desire to eventually coach internationally while insisting he remains content away from the touchline. "This is the first time I speak about this, but yes, I did talk to them," Guardiola said. "I felt embarrassed to say 'no' to Italy, a country like Italy, it would have been one of the greatest honours of my career to coach the Italian national team. But I realised I needed to stop. If they had called two years earlier, I probably would have accepted. "But when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom I love dearly, reached out, it was at a point where I simply had to stop. I needed some time for myself. After 18 years as a coach, with matches every three days, week in and week out, there comes a moment when you just have to say 'phew.'" Identifying "a national team" as his sole unfulfilled coaching ambition - and "that is the next step" for his career - Guardiola stressed he is in no rush to return. "The truth is, I don't know, I really don't know. But for now, I'm doing fine," he added. "If I ever return, it will be because my gut tells me to, and because someone wants me, then I'll go back. But it's been many years, so many matches." top.title: AGN mourns Pete Edochie, describes him as ‘father figure’
top.description: By Benjamin Njoku The National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Alhaji Abubakar Yakubu, has mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, describing him as a father figure in the Nigerian entertainment industry whose legacy would endure for generations. Edochie, 79, reportedly died in the early hours of Wednesday following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His son, Leo Pete Edochie, announced his death in an Instagram post, describing him as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.” In his tribute, Yakubu described the late actor as an all-rounder whose contributions extended beyond Nollywood to the broadcasting industry. “Pete Edochie was a man of the people, a detribalised Nigerian who spoke different languages. He lived a noble life, a dedicated Christian and a disciplinarian,” he said. He added that the actor’s death came at a time when the industry still needed his experience and contributions. “He died when the industry needed him most. But as a thorough-bred actor, he left when the ovation was loudest,” Yakubu said. Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, Edochie, fondly called Ebube Dike, hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State. He began his career in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation, where he rose to become Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. He gained national prominence in the 1980s through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart. The role earned him widespread recognition and helped launch a celebrated career in Nigerian cinema. Known for his deep voice, commanding delivery and rich use of proverbs, Edochie became synonymous with portrayals of kings, community leaders and family patriarchs. His notable film credits include Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart (2018), directed by Genevieve Nnaji. In recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry, he was honoured with the Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003, the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and several lifetime achievement honours. top.description: New manager, fresh hope. But why the stats say Al Faisaly don't need overhaul feature Mohamed Dahman replaces Giovanni Solinas in the dugout ahead of his debut match against fellow new boys Diriyah Club It might seem a rather obvious statement, but football is all about goals. The important distinction, however, is it is just as important to deny them as it is to score them. Just look at promoted sides Al Faisaly and Diriyah Club . Both started the 2026-27 Roshn Saudi League with different expectations and ambitions. Yet despite Diriyah Club signing Darwin Nunez , it is actually Al Faisaly that has scored the more goals this season out of the two - 13 goals to 10. The issue is, though, that Al Faisaly have conceded almost twice as many (24 to 13) and that is the story of their respective campaigns so far. Mohamed Dahman takes temporary charge of Al Faisaly following Giovanni Solinas' resignation There is much to like in how the Al Majma’ah-based side have played and, although manager Giovanni Solinas recently resigned, his interim replacement, Mohamed Dahman, inherits a squad that is already halfway there. At present, Al Faisaly are the league’s No.1-ranked pressing team, applying high-pressure to 46.3 percent of opposition touches, yet their opponents complete 79.2% of passes under that pressure. The former is proof they have the style right; they now just need to increase its effectiveness. That is, forcing more errors and turning the ball over more often. That’s easier said than done, of course, but it’s a better place to start than the alternative. Giovanni Solinas leaves Al Faisaly with the club one spot above the relegation zone The key focus for Dahman against Diriyah Club when the two RSL new boys meet in Matchweek 13 on Thursday must be on how the hosts start the game. That’s because the statistics reveal that Al Faisaly have conceded a league-high number of goals (14) in the first half. Drilling down even further, 13 of those have been conceded in the opening 30 minutes - also a league high - and eight between minutes 16 and 30. That latter? You guessed it, a league high. Contrast that to Diriyah Club, who are yet to give away a goal in the opening 15 minutes, and have conceded only six in the first half, and the contrast hits home. “We exploited the opposition’s defensive confusion after the first goal,” explained Al Fayha coach Fabio Carille late last month, after his team’s Sudair Derby success against Al Faisaly . So, for Al Faisaly, tightening their belts defensively must be priority No.1. That said, it’s not through lack of effort: they sit second for tackles and third for interceptions in the RSL this season. They’re pressing high, they’re winning tackles and intercepting the ball but, despite all of that, they still have the league’s third-worst defensive record. Yet it’s not all bad news. top.title: Pete Edochie: Nigeria has lost a voice that time will never silence — Pat Utomi
top.description: Political economist, Pat Utomi, has paid tribute to veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, describing him as a cultural institution whose legacy will endure beyond his lifetime. Utomi, in a tribute shared on his Facebook page on Wednesday, said Nigeria had lost a distinguished voice whose contributions to the country’s entertainment industry and cultural heritage would remain unforgettable. Describing Edochie as an iroko tree that had fallen, Utomi said the veteran actor’s departure was a monumental loss not only to the entertainment industry but also to generations who grew up watching his performances. “An iroko has fallen, Nigeria has lost a voice that time will never silence,” he wrote. He described Edochie as a custodian of African storytelling and a cultural institution whose commanding presence and performances had become part of Nigeria’s collective memory. Utomi particularly recalled the actor’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart, saying he brought the character to life and presented the depth and complexities of African civilisation to the world. “When Chief Pete Edochie stood before the camera as Okonkwo in Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, he did something extraordinary. He breathed life into a literary character and gave the world a glimpse into the depth, complexity, pride and contradictions of African civilisation,” he said. According to Utomi, Edochie did not merely interpret the character but immortalised it through his performance. He noted that the actor’s distinctive voice, commanding presence and dignified approach to his craft had earned him a special place in the hearts of audiences across generations. Beyond acting, Utomi acknowledged Edochie’s contributions to Nigerian broadcasting and cinema, saying his influence extended beyond entertainment and helped shape the country’s cultural landscape. He added that although the actor’s departure marked the end of a remarkable chapter, his legacy would continue through his films, the stories passed down to younger generations and the inspiration he provided to emerging actors. Utomi also extended his condolences to Edochie’s wife, children, family, friends and colleagues, praying that God would grant them the strength to bear the loss. “May your soul find eternal rest. Rest well, EBUBEDIKE!! Nigeria will never forget your legacy, Africa will speak your name till the end of time,” he added. nigeria.description: Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire on the importance of childhood financial literacy, the inspiration behind her book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , and her mission to raise a financially conscious generation. In a world where children are increasingly exposed to financial pressures, consumerism and unrealistic portrayals of wealth, teaching them how to manage money has become more important than ever. Yet, financial education remains largely absent from many children’s formative learning experiences. Following the launch of her children’s book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure , economist, financial literacy advocate and author, Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire, speaks about the personal experiences that inspired the book, why financial education must begin in childhood and her vision of making financial literacy accessible to children across Nigeria and Africa. Why should financial education begin in childhood? Interviewer: Financial literacy is increasingly becoming an important conversation among adults. Why are you making a case for introducing it to children? Ufuoma Paula: I believe we have waited too long to introduce children to conversations about money. We spend years teaching them how to read, write, calculate and prepare for examinations, but how much attention do we give to preparing them to make sound financial decisions? A child can graduate with excellent grades and still have no idea how to budget, save towards a goal, distinguish between needs and wants or manage money responsibly. Financial literacy is not something people suddenly need when they get their first salary. It is a life skill that is best developed early. Children already interact with money. They receive pocket money, make spending choices, compare what they own with what their friends have and develop attitudes towards money from what they observe at home and in society. Whether we deliberately teach them or not, they are learning something about money every day. The question is whether what they are learning is preparing them for responsible financial decisions. The lessons children learn about money today can influence the financial habits, values and decisions they carry into adulthood. Those decisions will affect not only their personal wellbeing, but also their families, businesses and communities. When we raise financially informed individuals, we are contributing to a society where people are better equipped to make responsible choices, recognise opportunities and manage resources wisely. We should teach children not just how to make money someday, but how to manage resources, recognise opportunities, create value and understand that money is a tool, not a master. nigeria.title: AGN mourns Pete Edochie, describes him as ‘father figure’
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku The National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Alhaji Abubakar Yakubu, has mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, describing him as a father figure in the Nigerian entertainment industry whose legacy would endure for generations. Edochie, 79, reportedly died in the early hours of Wednesday following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His son, Leo Pete Edochie, announced his death in an Instagram post, describing him as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.” In his tribute, Yakubu described the late actor as an all-rounder whose contributions extended beyond Nollywood to the broadcasting industry. “Pete Edochie was a man of the people, a detribalised Nigerian who spoke different languages. He lived a noble life, a dedicated Christian and a disciplinarian,” he said. He added that the actor’s death came at a time when the industry still needed his experience and contributions. “He died when the industry needed him most. But as a thorough-bred actor, he left when the ovation was loudest,” Yakubu said. Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, Edochie, fondly called Ebube Dike, hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State. He began his career in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation, where he rose to become Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. He gained national prominence in the 1980s through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart. The role earned him widespread recognition and helped launch a celebrated career in Nigerian cinema. Known for his deep voice, commanding delivery and rich use of proverbs, Edochie became synonymous with portrayals of kings, community leaders and family patriarchs. His notable film credits include Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart (2018), directed by Genevieve Nnaji. In recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry, he was honoured with the Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003, the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and several lifetime achievement honours. nigeria.title: No missing funds in $2.04bn Duke Oil crude cargoes — NNPC
nigeria.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has dismissed reports alleging that $2.04 billion realised from crude oil cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., was unaccounted for, insisting that all transactions were fully reconciled. The company said the $2.04 billion represented the gross value of 29 cargoes whose proceeds were set off against the cost of refined petroleum products supplied to Nigeria under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase (DSDP) programme. In a statement by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, NNPC said the absence of separate dollar receipts for some cargoes did not indicate missing funds. “No separate receipt appears because the crude sale proceeds were set off against the product purchase price, as the contracts provide,” it stated. Under the DSDP programme, participating traders lifted crude oil in exchange for refined petroleum products, including petrol, for the Nigerian market. NNPC explained that while crude was priced in dollars, products supplied were sold in naira, with transactions reconciled and captured in the audited financial statements of the relevant entities. The company said all 59 cargoes referenced in the reports were accounted for, adding that 30 were paid for in dollars, while proceeds from 28 cargoes, valued at approximately $1.96 billion, were remitted in naira to the NNPC Group Treasury or NNPC Upstream Investment Management Services accounts. The remaining cargo, a February 2023 Bonga tax-oil lifting valued at about $75.9 million, was paid into the then designated Federal Inland Revenue Service dollar account. On Duke Oil’s ownership, NNPC said it was incorporated in 1989 as its wholly owned trading subsidiary, adding that the relationship was documented in its corporate history, audited financial statements and NEITI’s 2023 industry report. It maintained that transactions between the company and its subsidiaries were disclosed as related-party transactions under International Financial Reporting Standards. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and accountability, but warned that it reserved the right to take legal action against publications it considered false or misleading. nigeria.title: Political Violence: Dying for nothing as a Nigerian politician?
nigeria.description: By Jide Ajani From the First Republic to the Fourth, politicians have been murdered, opposition figures silenced and political supporters killed. Yet, beyond the initial outrage, Nigeria has perfected the art of forgetting its dead. What, then, is the value of dying for a political cause in a country that cannot even preserve the memory of its political martyrs? The alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State, brings this odd reality into focus once again. Worse, many innocent, ordinary Nigerians have lost their lives while supporting or opposing politicians, only becoming part of an unidentified statistical figure. There is something inescapably tragic about dying while politicking in Nigeria. You could spend a lifetime building a political movement, challenging an unjust system, defending an electoral mandate, or fighting for an idea about your country’s future – or just being loud for nothing like a former, two-time state governor from the South West, or a former Rep and Senator from the North Central. You could become a household name, command enormous political influence and acquire a place in the nation’s history. Then, one morning, gunmen arrive, bullets are fired, and your life is terminated. There will be outrage. Condemnations will pour in. Politicians will issue statements, newspapers will publish editorials (like this), civil society organisations will demand justice, and the police will announce investigations. And then, Nigeria happens, and the people move on. The murder will become another entry in the country’s expanding archive of unresolved political crimes. The victim’s name will gradually disappear from public conversations, except when anniversary commemorations provide an opportunity for political speeches. Even the circumstances of the death may eventually become blurred by competing narratives, political expediency and the convenient amnesia of a nation. Is it, therefore, worth dying for Nigeria’s politics? The question intends to interrogate a society that celebrates political martyrs without demonstrating a corresponding commitment to preserving their legacies or establishing the truth about their deaths. nigeria.title: NRS seeks simpler tax rules for creative sector
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to unlock investment opportunities in Nigeria’s creative economy, stressing the need for a tax system that supports innovation, enterprise growth and wealth creation. The Service noted that the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions required regulations that creators, entrepreneurs and investors could easily understand and navigate. Speaking at the just concluded high-level dialogue on taxation and investment in the creative economy during the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) event in Lagos, Executive Chairman of the NRS, Dr. Zacch Adedeji, described the creative economy as one of Nigeria’s most promising economic assets, noting that it had evolved beyond entertainment into a major source of employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment and economic opportunities. Adedeji who was represented by the Executive Director, People, Stakeholders and Communication, Mr. Obinna Ihedioha, also said that digital platforms had transformed how creative value was produced and commercialised, with entrepreneurs building businesses around copyrights, designs, brands and digital products. He reiterated that tax administration must evolve to accommodate these developments without discouraging innovation or business expansion. “The government needs sustainable revenue to invest in education, security, technology and infrastructure. But how we tax matters as much as what we collect. It shapes whether businesses start, whether investors come, and whether enterprises grow or stay small,” he said. Adedeji added that the new tax laws offered an opportunity to establish a more efficient system through clearer regulations, reduced compliance burdens for small businesses and improved taxpayer support. He identified clarity, understanding and value as essential to effective taxation, stressing that formalisation should provide creative businesses with tangible benefits, including access to finance, contracts, investment, wider markets and legal protection. The NRS, he said, participated in CANEX through a high-level dialogue, an Investment and Tax Advisory Hub for creators and investors, and the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative (CETII), designed to sustain engagement beyond the event. nigeria.title: Petrol imports crash 52% as crude, wheat top Lagos ports
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse Imports of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), also known as petrol, through Lagos ports plunged by 52.23 per cent in November, while crude oil and bulk wheat ranked among the leading commodities imported through the ports in October and November. According to the Shipping Position document obtained from the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), PMS imports fell to 73,895 metric tonnes in November from 328,231 metric tonnes recorded in October. Crude oil imports through Lagos ports also dropped sharply, with 702,254 metric tonnes recorded in October, while no crude oil import was recorded in November. Bulk wheat ranked among the major commodities imported through Lagos ports during the period, with a combined 461,190 metric tonnes recorded in September, October and November. The breakdown showed that wheat imports rose to 252,348 metric tonnes in October and declined by 17.24 per cent to 208,842 metric tonnes in November. Other commodities on the import chart included 402,126 metric tonnes of PMS, 209,000 metric tonnes of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel, 212,700 metric tonnes of bulk sugar, 150,000 metric tonnes of aviation fuel and 114,263 metric tonnes of bulk salt. Bulk sugar imports stood at 109,350 metric tonnes in October and 103,400 metric tonnes in November, while bulk salt imports rose from 33,000 metric tonnes to 81,263 metric tonnes over the same period. The document also showed that 624 trucks, 157 transformers and three Rubber-Tyred Gantry (RTG) cranes were received through Lagos ports during the period under review. entertainment.title: How Williams Alamu Graduated with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan
entertainment.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. The thought of getting a B or C frightened me so much that I eventually decided not to sit for the examinations. entertainment.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. I have probably said that last part a hundred times since getting my results, and honestly, I don’t think I’m tired of saying it yet. Haha! One thing about me is that I like to be involved. I am sometimes curious about things that have absolutely nothing to do with what I’m supposed to be doing, and I genuinely enjoy working with people. I like organising things, bringing people together, and seeing an idea move forward to get accomplished. So I have known that going to Oxford was never going to be just about getting a master’s degree. Let me explain how I ended up there. Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. sports.title: How to unearth young stars, the Bayern Munich way
sports.description: Bayern initially aim to find young players from Bavaria before looking further afield [Getty Images] Bayern Munich are one of the elite powers in European football and current home of Ballon d'Or winner and England captain Harry Kane. But, while Kane is the latest hugely successful foreign import at Bayern, the German giants also put a particular focus on producing their own elite young talent. In 2013, Bayern had four homegrown players in the starting line-up as they won the Champions League. Repeating that victory, and continuing the club's history of nurturing young players, is what director of youth development and campus Jochen Sauer says Bayern are aiming for. Sauer joined from RB Salzburg in 2017 when the academy campus opened in another part of Munich, away from the first-team training complex. The club's motto "Mia San Mia" translates to "we are who we are" and Sauer says it has always been the club's goal to have a local homegrown element in its senior side. "It was always our identity and philosophy to be a regional club, but at the same time to be competitive internationally and on Champions League level," Sauer tells BBC Sport. "But always having a core of our team coming from the Munich area and the Bavarian region with a deep identification with the club and the city. "Our recruitment guidelines, especially for the under-11 to the under-15 teams, is trying to recruit as much talent as possible from the Munich area and the region of Bavaria." Munich-born Croatia international Josip Stanisic is a good example. The midfielder, 26, signed as an under-17 player from local outfit SC Furstenfeldbruck, while 22-year-old Aleksandar Pavlovic joined the academy aged eight and has worked his way up to the first team and is a Germany international. But perhaps the biggest name to come out of the academy in recent times is Jamal Musiala. The former Chelsea youth player, who joined aged 16, is a star for Bayern and Germany and has already won six Bundesliga titles at just 23 years old. It was part of the club's strategy to bring in the best young foreign players, and those with German passports, to the club, but they also enjoyed a bit of luck. The move came around the time Bayern Munich were interested in then-Chelsea winger Callum Hudson-Odoi, who shared the same agent as Musiala, who moved from Germany to England when he was seven. Bayern were already aware of Musiala because he was born in Germany, but the timing was right to make a deal happen. "There were for sure some pieces that came together at that time," Sauer says. sports.description: Eduard Löwen powers San Jose to first playoff win in 14 years By Harrison Hamm San Jose Earthquakes fans have been awaiting this moment for a generation. In the first-ever Audi MLS Cup Playoffs game at PayPal Park on Tuesday night, summer signing Eduard Löwen delivered a stunning long-range free kick that proved the difference in the Quakes' 2-1 win over Houston Dynamo FC , just a day after being named the 2026 MLS Comeback Player of the Year . The Game 1 victory in their Western Conference Round One Best-of-3 Series marked San Jose's first Audi MLS Cup Playoffs since 2012 and puts the Earthquakes one win away from advancing in the postseason for the first time since 2010. “We had a really good performance,” Löwen told Apple TV postgame. “We played well. We were the better team." Lovely Löwen With San Jose leading 1-0 courtesy of captain Ronaldo Vieira 's first MLS goal, Löwen unleashed one of the most impressive strikes of the playoffs so far. His free kick from distance caromed in off the post past Jonathan Bond , mere minutes after Bond had made a diving stop to deny another Löwen free kick. “It's definitely high up,” Löwen said of where the goal ranks in his career tallies. “It's definitely high up in the category. I'm thankful that the second one went in. Credit to the goalkeeper on the first one. That was an amazing save, and I thought I'd go the same way again. But then I thought maybe I'd try the other way." Since being acquired in August from St. Louis CITY SC , Löwen has established himself as an integral piece of the Quakes’ midfield, as he proved at both ends of the pitch on Tuesday night with a goal-line clearance to preserve San Jose's lead shortly before going on to double the advantage with his first playoff goal. Löwen's success in San Jose follows a time of significant personal adversity during which he stepped away from professional soccer last year to care for his wife, Ilona, who passed away in March after two years of brain cancer treatment. The German playmaker returned to the sport this season and has excelled, earning recognition as the Comeback Player of the Year. Now, he is helping lead the way as the Quakes look to go somewhere they haven’t been in more than a decade. “Everything’s new here,” legendary head coach Bruce Arena said after the game. “We’re learning to be a good club. We’re learning to be a good team. Anything where we’re moving in a good direction is positive.” Headed to Houston San Jose can close out the Round One Best-of-3 Series in Game 2 on Saturday at Shell Energy Stadium in Houston, where a win would send them to the Western Conference Semifinals (2:30 pm ET | Apple TV ). sports.title: Why The NFL Is Bringing U2 And Wu-Tang Clan To Thanksgiving Football
sports.description: The NFL logo is seen on the field. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty Images The NFL on Thanksgiving isn’t going to challenge the Super Bowl anytime soon But Thanksgiving offers something the Super Bowl does not: multiple games, more entertainment and a direct connection to holiday shopping. This year, for the first time, the NFL will air games on Thanksgiving Eve, Thanksgiving and Black Friday. And the games will create a large-scale entertainment platform for Wu-Tang Clan, U2, Miranda Lambert, and the Goo Goo Dolls, all of whom are performing in some capacity amid the five (count ‘em, five) games blitzing streaming and linear broadcast networks. The festivities begin when the Packers and Rams clash in the inaugural Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix. Here’s why the NFL on Thanksgiving is now the place to see the band that changed rap forever with Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers) : the NFL has already won the battle for sports fans. Thanksgiving week is about the NFL embedding itself into popular culture through entertainment and commerce, which attracts viewers beyond sports enthusiasts. From Doubleheaders to Dolly Parton The NFL has come a long way since Thanksgiving meant watching the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys square off against different opponents on network TV with nothing particularly noteworthy happening at halftime. Dolly Parton creating a cultural moment (and arguably eclipsing the game itself) by appearing in a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader uniform as she did in 2023 was unthinkable. But the tradition began to change over a period of years, beginning when the NFL added a third Thanksgiving game in 2006. The rise of streaming was the catalyst that pushed the NFL to another level of entertainment and football. The launch of Amazon’s Black Friday game in 2023 marked the first time the NFL expanded its holiday programming beyond Thanksgiving Day. And that year, the NFL began a sustained pattern of promoting three major musical headliners across all three Thanksgiving Day games. The streaming businesses have had good reason to muscle their way into the Thanksgiving tradition. Every elite or contending team is looking to build their offence around a world-class QB and their defence around a world-class edge rusher. Defensive players usually play within a system, so the EDGE is the one defender who is designed to be an independent unit responsible for sacking a slow QB. sports.description: Bournemouth v Manchester City - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Pep Guardiola has broken his silence on his decision to turn down the opportunity to manage Italy, admitting he felt "embarrassed" to say no to the Azzurri. The legendary tactician, currently on a sabbatical following a trophy-laden decade at Manchester City, also confirmed that his next move in football will be onto the international stage. Italy approached Guardiola after third straight World Cup miss In July, after Italy missed a third consecutive World Cup, the Italian federation (FIGC) sent Paolo Maldini and Leonardo to approach Guardiola . The offer arrived shortly after he left Manchester City following a 2016–2026 stint yielding six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and a Champions League crown. Drained by the grind, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich manager chose a self-imposed sabbatical of at least one year. Italy subsequently re-hired Roberto Mancini , their Euro 2020-winning coach from 2018 to 2023. Guardiola opens up on emotional Azzurri refusal Speaking on Romario TV on Tuesday with Brazil legend and former Barcelona team-mate Romario, Guardiola explained why timing scuppered the Italy move. He also confirmed his desire to eventually coach internationally while insisting he remains content away from the touchline. "This is the first time I speak about this, but yes, I did talk to them," Guardiola said. "I felt embarrassed to say 'no' to Italy, a country like Italy, it would have been one of the greatest honours of my career to coach the Italian national team. But I realised I needed to stop. If they had called two years earlier, I probably would have accepted. "But when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom I love dearly, reached out, it was at a point where I simply had to stop. I needed some time for myself. After 18 years as a coach, with matches every three days, week in and week out, there comes a moment when you just have to say 'phew.'" Identifying "a national team" as his sole unfulfilled coaching ambition - and "that is the next step" for his career - Guardiola stressed he is in no rush to return. "The truth is, I don't know, I really don't know. But for now, I'm doing fine," he added. "If I ever return, it will be because my gut tells me to, and because someone wants me, then I'll go back. Both started the 2026-27 Roshn Saudi League with different expectations and ambitions. Mohamed Dahman takes temporary charge of Al Faisaly following Giovanni Solinas' resignation There is much to like in how the Al Majma’ah-based side have played and, although manager Giovanni Solinas recently resigned, his interim replacement, Mohamed Dahman, inherits a squad that is already halfway there. At present, Al Faisaly are the league’s No.1-ranked pressing team, applying high-pressure to 46.3 percent of opposition touches, yet their opponents complete 79.2% of passes under that pressure. The former is proof they have the style right; they now just need to increase its effectiveness. That is, forcing more errors and turning the ball over more often. That’s easier said than done, of course, but it’s a better place to start than the alternative. Giovanni Solinas leaves Al Faisaly with the club one spot above the relegation zone The key focus for Dahman against Diriyah Club when the two RSL new boys meet in Matchweek 13 on Thursday must be on how the hosts start the game. Contrast that to Diriyah Club, who are yet to give away a goal in the opening 15 minutes, and have conceded only six in the first half, and the contrast hits home. “We exploited the opposition’s defensive confusion after the first goal,” explained Al Fayha coach Fabio Carille late last month, after his team’s Sudair Derby success against Al Faisaly . So, for Al Faisaly, tightening their belts defensively must be priority No.1. sports.description: Nov 24, 2026; Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; The Vegas Golden Knights celebrate a goal by forward Trevor Connelly (24) during the first period against the Edmonton Oilers at Rogers Place. EDMONTON—It is almost shocking that Trevor Connelly is not discussed more often when discussing favorites for the Calder Trophy. While there are certainly deserving candidates, Connelly has consistently stayed at or near the top among all rookies in goals and points.
